title: Why we don't fly off the spinning Earth
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why doesn't the spinning Earth throw us off?
How fast is the Earth spinning?
Why can't we feel the Earth move?

items.label: Pull to keep circling
items.ask: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?

explain.say: The Earth spins once a day, so at the equator you are carried round at about 1,670 kilometres per hour. To keep moving in a circle instead of flying off in a straight line, you need a pull towards the centre.

draw.text: Why we don't fly off the spinning Earth

items.label: Pull to keep circling
items.ask: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?

explain.say: Because the Earth is so big, its circle is huge and gentle. The pull needed to keep you circling is tiny, only about a third of a percent of the pull of gravity.

items.label: Pull to keep circling
items.ask: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?

explain.say: Gravity pulls you towards the centre about 290 times harder than that. It easily supplies the small pull for the circle and has plenty left over to hold you firmly on the ground.

items.label: Pull to keep circling
items.ask: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?

explain.say: The spin does make you a tiny bit lighter at the equator than at the poles. Even on the Moon, where gravity is about a sixth of Earth's, its slow spin could never throw you off.

items.label: Pull to keep circling
items.ask: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?

faq.a: Earth's gravity makes falling things speed up by about 9.8 metres per second every second, which scientists write as 9.8 metres per second squared.

faq.q: What would happen if the Earth spun much faster?
faq.a: If the Earth spun about 17 times faster, a day would last less than an hour and a half, and at the equator gravity would only just keep things circling. Objects there would become almost weightless.
asks: Could the Earth spin fast enough to throw us off?

faq.q: Why don't we feel the Earth spinning?
faq.a: We, the air and everything around us move along with the Earth at a steady speed. You only feel motion when it speeds up, slows down or turns sharply, and the Earth turns smoothly, just once a day.
asks: Why can't I feel the Earth move?

faq.q: How fast is the Earth spinning?
faq.a: At the equator the ground moves at about 1,670 kilometres per hour. Nearer the poles the circle is smaller, so the speed is less, and at the poles you just turn on the spot.
asks: How fast are we moving as the Earth spins?

faq.q: Are you lighter at the equator?
faq.a: Yes, slightly. A little of gravity's pull is used to carry you round the circle, and the Earth bulges at the equator, so you are further from its centre. Together these make you about half a percent lighter there than at the poles.
asks: Do you weigh less at the equator?

facts: The Earth spins once every 23 hours 56 minutes relative to the stars.
At the equator, the Earth's surface moves at about 1,670 kilometres per hour.
Gravity is about 9.83 metres per second squared at the poles and about 9.78 at the equator.

quiz.say: Why don't we get flung off the spinning Earth?
quiz.show: We stay on the spinning Earth because…

options.show: Gravity is far stronger than the pull needed to keep us circling
options.say: Gravity is far stronger than the pull needed to keep us circling

options.show: The Earth is not really spinning
options.say: The Earth is not really spinning

quiz.why: Keeping you on the Earth's huge, gentle circle needs only a tiny pull, and gravity is about 290 times stronger than that.

wrong.1: Air pressure pushes equally in all directions; gravity holds us down.
wrong.2: The Earth does spin, once a day; that is what gives us day and night.
